title: Find Kth Bit in Nth Binary String
summary: Given two positive integers n and k , the binary string S_n is constructed as follows: - S_1 = "0" - For i > 1 , S_i = S_{i-1} + "1" + reverse(invert(S_{i-1})) Here, + denotes string concatenation, reverse(x) returns the reversed string x , and invert(x) inverts all the bits in x (changing 0 to 1 and 1 to 0).
statement: Given two positive integers n and k , the binary string S_n is constructed as follows: - S_1 = "0" - For i > 1 , S_i = S_{i-1} + "1" + reverse(invert(S_{i-1})) Here, + denotes string concatenation, reverse(x) returns the reversed string x , and invert(x) inverts all the bits in x (changing 0 to 1 and 1 to 0). For example, the first four strings in the sequence are: - S_1 = "0" - S_2 = "011" - S_3 = "0111001" - S_4 = "011100110110001" Return the k -th bit in S_n . It is guaranteed that k is within the valid range for the given n .
constraints: S1 is 0; each later string is the prior string, then 1, then the reversed bitwise inverse of the prior string.
Return the one-based kth bit of Sn without constructing the exponential-length string.
reference_solution:
def kth_recursive_binary_bit(n, k):
 if n==1:return '0'
 middle=1<<(n-1)
 if k==middle:return '1'
 if k<middle:return kth_recursive_binary_bit(n-1,k)
 bit=kth_recursive_binary_bit(n-1,(1<<n)-k)
 return '1' if bit=='0' else '0'

hints: The string length is 2^n-1 and its center is position 2^(n-1).
Positions left of center recurse unchanged into Sn-1.
Positions right of center reflect to 2^n-k in Sn-1 and invert the returned bit.
These cases follow directly from prefix, center, and reversed-inverted suffix construction.
